title: Warden Coverage for Every Repo Toolchain Process and Disk-Bounded Swap
description: The Mac worker ran out of application memory and macOS halted it, while the host warden (ticket 26/11/24/FLEET-MEMORY-WATCHDOG-ADMISSION-AND-UNIT-CARVING) stayed calm and acted on nothing. Cause: warden subjects must descend from a bun root or the build scheduler, so rustc/cargo started by shell scripts (native fallback builds, agents' cargo test runs, rustc-wrapper bypass) and cargo test binaries and Playwright browsers were invisible; those scripts also ran -j 8 without admission; and the disk had filled to 95%, capping macOS swap at 3 GB. This must never happen: every memory-relevant process launched from the repo's pinned toolchains, repo target directories or repo browser runtime must be a warden subject regardless of ancestry; native cargo invocations must pass the host-capacity admission and the rustc wrapper instead of bypassing them; the warden's level must account for swap headroom bounded by free disk; packages whose compile units exceed the 16 GB-class unit ceiling must be carved. Language-agnostic tests with an independent oracle; proof on this worker.
